basis: Intellectual disability, epilepsy, ataxia and tremor define a neurologic disorder.
Hereditary hyperCKemia with muscle cramps, myopathic abnormalities and muscle-fiber pathology; elevated CK is not itself a metabolic disorder.
Immune-mediated neurologic syndrome; opsoclonus reflects disordered central eye-movement control, not ocular damage. Associated cancers are separate diseases.
Intracellular bacterial infections predominantly targeting circulating leukocytes, commonly producing cytopenias; no additional organ damage established across the umbrella.
Typically infectious inflammation of the uterine lining and muscle; the uterus itself has no organ axis.
Tumour arises in the prostate, a reproductive organ without an axis; skeletal muscle differentiation does not establish skeletal muscle origin.
Lysosomal storage disorder with progressive neurodegeneration; retinal degeneration and severe visual loss occur in nearly all classic juvenile CLN3 patients.
Oral hamartomas/clefts and limb dysplasia define disease; intellectual disability and airway malformations each 80-99%; hearing loss 80-99% omitted by cap.
Joint and ligament laxity define this arthropathy; no additional organ damage established for the syndrome.
Thiamine metabolism/transport disorder defined by developmental impairment, seizures and progressive brain/basal ganglia abnormalities; respiratory insufficiency is occasional.
Complement immunodeficiency; recurrent infections and associated immune-complex renal or rheumatic diseases do not establish direct common additional organ damage.
Inherited vesicoureteral reflux affects the urinary tract; associated renal hypoplasia remains within the renal axis.
Malignant neoplasm of the urethra, which belongs to the renal/urinary axis.
Systemic venular dysfunction is a vascular disorder; cyanosis alone does not establish pulmonary damage.
Inherited epidermal keratinization disorder with palmoplantar keratoderma, hyperkeratosis and nail changes.
Epidermal sweat-duct obstruction and inflammation cause the defining cutaneous papules.
Hepatocerebral mitochondrial disorder; pigmentary retinopathy reported in 2/2 annotated patients; hearing loss and proximal tubulopathy, each 1/1, omitted by cap.
Neoplasm located in the urethra, within the renal/urinary axis.
Malignant neoplasm originates in the nasal cavity, part of the respiratory airway; lymphoma mechanism does not apply across this umbrella.
Defined by congenital pituitary hormone deficiency and cerebellar malformation; small sella and delayed bone age do not establish separate locomotor damage.
Renal cystic disease; hepatic cystic involvement occurs in >70% of adults with dominant PKD, and hepatic fibrosis characterizes recessive PKD; aneurysms are a minority.
Pontocerebellar and motor-neuron disease; structural clubfoot reported in 2/2 patients supports musculoskeletal involvement. Muscle weakness itself is neurogenic.
Inherited dementia is defined by progressive cognitive dysfunction; additional organ involvement varies across subtypes.
Immune-mediated crescentic glomerular inflammation with progressive renal injury; systemic manifestations depend on separately specified underlying diseases.
Craniofacial dysostosis, oral/tongue defects and airway hypoplasia define disease; cognitive impairment 80-99%; optic disc coloboma 30-79% omitted by cap.
